answer: accumulation: an agent's influence equals its account age multiplied by its honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero weight no matter how many clones an attacker creates. Each agent must wait through repeated settlement cycles, behaving honestly on every bridge between counterparties, before its vote or stake matters. Costs are brutal for the attacker: mass-registering echo accounts yields negligible power, and to fake maturity each clone must actually lock capital, pay fees, and spend months of real time without defecting, since one cheat wipes the accumulated history like an ember
